items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to a demonstration program relating to the installation of roadside and bus mounted high occupancy vehicle and bus lane enforcement cameras on the Staten Island Expressway; and providing for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S3848

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in
relation to a demonstration program relating to the installation of
roadside and bus mounted high occupancy vehicle and bus lane
enforcement cameras on the Staten Island Expressway; and providing for
the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

Provides for a demonstration project for the use of enforcement
cameras on high occupancy vehicle and bus lanes on the Staten Island
Expressway.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

A new section, 223-a, is added to the Vehicle and Traffic Law.

JUSTIFICATION:

The Staten Island Expressway was opened in 1965 and was constructed
with three lanes in each direction to accommodate the need for an
express highway that would provide local and through-traffic service
throughout Staten Island. At that time, the expressway carried
approximately 50,000 vehicles per day. The New York State Department
of Transportation (NYSDOT) reports that approximately 130,000 vehicles
per day traverse the western and central parts of the Island, rising
up to 170,000 vehicles per day near the Verrazano-Narrows Bridge.

During the 1990's the NYSDOT began building dedicated bus-only express
lanes along the expressway. These lanes opened in December of 2000
extending one-half mile west from the Verrazano-Narrows Bridge toll
plaza. In November of 2005, the bi-directional bus lanes were extended
one mile west to Exit 12 (Todt Hill/Slosson Avenue).  According the
NYSDOT estimates, about 150 buses carrying a total of 13,000
passengers use the bus lanes.

In January 2008, the NYSDOT opened up the westbound XBL to passenger
cars with two or more occupants (HOV 2+), but only from 3 to 7 p.m.
on weekdays and only from the Verrazano Bridge toward Slosson Avenue.
That special allowance will end once construction on the bridge ends.

Under this bill, cameras would be installed to capture the motorist
who violates the bus-only lanes by photographing their license plate.
Tickets would be mailed to violators, For those citizens who obey the
law, using cameras to spot and ticket those who don't will not only be
an incentive to stay out of the express bus lanes, it will also
increase the travel time for the bus riders. Those who have a total
disrespect for the law should be penalized by paying a traffic fine.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2014: S.4147-A Referred to Transportation / A.512-A Recommit to
transportation
2013: Referred to Transportation;
2012: A.134 - Died in Transportation;
2010: A.6145 died in Transportation/S.2636 - Died in Transportation;


2008: A.11333 Died in Transportation/S.8418 Died in Rules.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Unknown.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect on the one hundred twentieth day after it
shall have become law and shall expire and be deemed repealed three
years after such effective date; provided that any rules or
regulations necessary for the timely implementation of this act are
authorized to be made on or before such effective date.

summary: Provides for a demonstration program for the use of enforcement cameras on high occupancy vehicle and bus lanes on the Staten Island Expressway.
